language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

translation.text:
<warning>The OCR transcriber could not read the Mongolian body text. The photo was low-resolution and the red ink was faded. The unread regions are kept as unclear below and have not been reconstructed. A full-resolution or cropped image is needed for a reliable transcription and translation.</warning>
<meta>Page number 二 (2). Header in Chinese: 諸品經第二卷上二, "Zhupin jing <note>Sutra of Various Classes, a Chinese label for a section of the Mongolian Kanjur</note>, volume 2, upper part, folio 2." The source is a red-ink woodblock print inside a double-ruled frame, probably from the Beijing Mongolian Kanjur of 1718–1720.</meta>

<term>Zhupin jing</term> <gloss>Sutra of Various Classes</gloss>, volume two, upper part, folio two

<margin><unclear>short Mongolian marginal label (about 4 words), probably section/folio indicator, not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<unclear>about 24 columns of Classical Mongolian text in Uighur-Mongol script, printed in red ink; not legible at the available resolution, not transcribed</unclear>

<note>A rectangular double-ruled frame surrounds the text block. It is filled with a fine scrolling floral border in arabesque style. Narrow panels at the left and right, with ornamental corner motifs, hold the marginal labels. Red-ink printing like this was often used for imperial editions of Buddhist scripture.</note>

<summary>This is folio 2 of the upper part of volume 2 of a section labelled in Chinese as the Zhupin jing, from a red-ink Mongolian woodblock print of the Buddhist canon. The Mongolian text could not be read at the available resolution, so only the Chinese margin label and the decorative frame are rendered.</summary>
<keywords>Zhupin jing, Mongolian Kanjur, Beijing Kanjur, Classical Mongolian, Uighur-Mongol script, red-ink woodblock print, Buddhist canon, pothi leaf, illegible text</keywords>
